title: The Passage of Mount Kessler
premise: Felix Joubert, a bush pilot who has spent a decade outrunning his past one flight at a time, discovers a cave exposed by an unprecedented low tide on the Kessler coast — and inside it, evidence that the region's founding family built their fortune on something buried and deliberately forgotten. When the powerful Kessler heir joins Felix's small expedition under a false name, loyalty to his crew collides with the truth of what they find: a ledger proving the family's wealth was bought with a covered-up disaster that killed dozens. As calving season closes in and the glacier route home becomes passable for only days, Felix must decide whether to fly the evidence out and destroy the family that now owns everything he depends on, or bury the cave again and keep his people safe. He chooses truth, flying out through the collapsing ice with the ledger while the expedition seals the cave behind them — ending with the story published, Felix grounded but finally standing still, and the mountain holding its silence no longer.
about_author: Wren Vasquez is the pen name of a former floatplane mechanic who spent six seasons in coastal Alaska before turning to writing full-time. Their fiction draws on firsthand knowledge of bush aviation and the quiet moral bargains of remote communities.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Felix Joubert flies medicine and gossip between coastal settlements, establishing his routine, his battered de Havilland, and his habit of never staying anywhere long enough to owe anyone anything. A radio warning about record-low tides goes unheeded. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: restless contentment masking avoidance.

chapters.title: What the Tide Left
chapters.summary: On a supply run to Kessler Point, Felix spots a cave mouth revealed by the freak tide, its walls bearing carved marks too deliberate to be natural. His passenger, marine biologist Ines Okafor, begs him to land. They explore briefly and find a rusted strongbox fused into the rock. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into unease.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Ines pries the strongbox open in Felix's hangar: inside is a company ledger from 1911 recording wages paid to workers who, cross-referenced against town records, all died in a single undocumented winter. The last entry names a Kessler. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: A Passenger Named Ash
chapters.summary: A well-dressed stranger calling himself Ash Corrigan hires Felix for a private charter to the point, asking oddly specific questions about the cave. Felix recognizes the family jawline beneath the alias — this is Elias Kessler III. He says nothing, and takes the money. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: complicity chosen in real time.

chapters.title: Crew of Four
chapters.summary: Ines recruits her brother Tomas, a glacier guide, and old friend Ruthie Calloway, a journalist itching to leave obituaries behind. The five agree to a proper expedition before calving season opens the ice route — three weeks away. Ash volunteers, claiming survey experience. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: fragile camaraderie built on a secret half-kept.

chapters.title: Provisions and Prevarications
chapters.summary: Preparations expose fault lines: Ruthie senses a story being managed, Tomas distrusts Ash instantly, and Felix quietly buys a second fuel cache without telling anyone why. Elias, meanwhile, makes a call from a payphone, and someone answers. POV: Elias/Ash. Emotional beat: everyone lying a little, for different reasons.

chapters.title: Up the Ice Road
chapters.summary: The team treks inland along the glacier's frozen margin toward the cave's upper entrance, which Ines believes exists based on the tide cave's airflow. Tomas leads across crevassed ground; Ash proves competent and likable, unsettling Felix further. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: trust extended as a calculated risk.

chapters.title: The Upper Mouth
chapters.summary: They find the upper entrance behind a rockfall and descend into chambers lined with the same carvings — a tally, hundreds deep. Deeper still: collapsed timber, old tools, and a sealed gallery the ledger seems to describe. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: awe giving way to horror at scale.

chapters.title: Tally of the Lost
chapters.summary: Ruthie deciphers the tally: one mark per worker entombed by a deliberately collapsed tunnel during the winter of 1911 — two hundred and eleven marks. Elias, alone in a side chamber, photographs documents and pockets a fragment. POV: Ruthie. Emotional beat: grief for strangers, and the weight of witness.

chapters.title: Ash Breaks
chapters.summary: Felix confronts Elias privately in camp. Elias confesses his identity and claims he came to expose his own family — then asks Felix to help him remove the ledger quietly, 'to protect the descendants of the dead.' Felix doesn't believe him. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: sympathy weaponized.

chapters.title: Stormbound
chapters.summary: An early storm pins them in the cave mouth for two days. Stripped of distraction, the group argues about what the discovery owes anyone: publication, restitution, or silence. Ruthie notices Elias's missing document fragment. POV: Ruthie. Emotional beat: the expedition's unity cracking under pressure.

chapters.title: The First Betrayal
chapters.summary: Elias slips out at night to mark the cave for a follow-up crew he arranged weeks ago; Tomas catches him returning. Confronted, Elias reveals a satellite phone and admits his family's lawyers are already moving to claim the site as private land. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: betrayal confirmed, fury contained.

chapters.title: Whose Truth Is It
chapters.summary: The group debates destroying the evidence to spite the Keslers versus getting it out. Ines argues the dead deserve names, not leverage. Felix realizes whichever choice they make, someone will be sacrificed — possibly all of them. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: idealism tested against survival math.

chapters.title: Calving Season Opens
chapters.summary: The storm breaks; the glacier begins shedding. The ice route home is open — for perhaps four days. Radio contact reveals a Kessler-chartered survey plane inbound, meaning the window is even shorter than they thought. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the clock becoming a character.

chapters.title: Splitting the Party
chapters.summary: They divide the evidence: Ruthie carries copies of the ledger pages overland with Tomas as insurance; Felix and Ines take the original by air with Elias as reluctant hostage-guest. Each pair knows the other might be caught. POV: Tomas. Emotional beat: trust made structural, not sentimental.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: Felix's plane won't start — sabotage, almost certainly by whoever answered Elias's call. Stranded at the coast strip, Felix and Ines improvise repairs while the survey plane circles. Elias, watching his family close the net, begins genuinely helping. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: desperation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Overland Gamble
chapters.summary: Tomas and Ruthie race the softening ice road as meltwater opens crevasses early. A bridge collapse forces a detour through the tide cave itself, racing the rising water with the copied ledger in a dry bag. POV: Ruthie. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Flight Through Falling Ice
chapters.summary: Felix gets the engine running and lifts off through the calving field as seracs collapse around the strip, Elias navigating from the right seat because he knows the family's patrol patterns. They thread the corridor and clear the coast as the route closes behind them. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: ten years of flight distilled into one that matters.

chapters.title: Reckoning at Kessler House
chapters.summary: Rather than flee, Felix lands at the Kessler estate strip and walks the ledger up the drive, Elias beside him. confronted by his father, Elias chooses publicly: he hands the original to Ruthie, arriving by boat, and resigns his name on camera. POV: Elias. Emotional beat: inheritance refused.

chapters.title: Names for the Dead
chapters.summary: The story breaks nationally. Researchers reopen the cave legally; the two hundred and eleven names go up in the Kessler Point church. Some townspeople resent the disruption; others bring flowers to the shore. Tomas guides the first official party in. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: truth landing unevenly, but landing.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Keeps
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the fallout settles: lawsuits, a foundation in the workers' names, Elias estranged and lighter for it. Felix learns the cave has already begun closing naturally — the sea reclaiming it. Some answers, he reflects, were always meant to be temporary. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: peace with impermanence.

chapters.title: One More Mile
chapters.summary: Final chapter: Felix takes a last flight over the point, drops a wreath at the tide line, and — for the first time in ten years — files a return trip. He lands, stays the night, and lets someone wait for him. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: choosing to be found.
